intro.line: Tarkir. A world of steppes, mountains and ice, ruled by five warrior clans and their khans.
There were dragons here once. The clans hunted them until there were none. Now there are only bones.
Sarkhan Vol was born here, and left, and served Nicol Bolas, and lost his mind on Zendikar. He has come home because a voice keeps calling him.
Unwelcome thoughts crowd my mind. Are they my own madness, or the whispers of another?

finale.line: More than a thousand years ago, Bolas left Ugin for dead. Sarkhan wrapped the broken dragon in a hedron and kept him alive. That one act changed everything after it.
The dragon tempests never stopped. The dragons never died. The five clans became the servants of five Dragonlords.
Dragons in the skies of Tarkir—for the first time, it feels like my home.
Even paradise is not without tragedies.
Ugin still sleeps in his hedron, alive. In this Tarkir, Narset is a planeswalker. And for the first time in years, the voice in Sarkhan's head is quiet.

villainFinale.line: Silumgar coils on his hoard and does not even look up.
Silumgar never passes up an opportunity to add to his opulence.
Bring forth the dead, their skull-grins and rattle-bones. We will feast upon their wailing ghosts.
Sarkhan got exactly what he wanted. A world full of dragons. He forgot to ask what the dragons would want.

battles.title: Qal Sisma
battles.blurb: You arrive in the frozen mountains of Qal Sisma, where Surrak, khan of the Temur, has caught an Abzan war party on his side of the pass. Anafenza leads them herself.

scene.line: Hold the high ground, then bring it to your enemy.
People are often humbled by the elements. But the elements, too, can be humbled.
Ferocious: some Temur cards get a bonus if you control a creature with power 4 or greater. Get a big one down first.

villainScene.line: Stand where the whole battle can see you. Strike so they'll never forget.
Rarely at rest on the Amber Throne, Anafenza always leads the Abzan Houses to battle.

after.line: A man came through the pass last week talking to himself about dragons. Vol, his name was. Of the Mardu, once. Zurgo wants him dead.

battles.title: The Way of the Jeskai
battles.blurb: Narset, khan of the Jeskai, studies the old dragons in secret, and Sarkhan has heard she knows where the voice is coming from. Sidisi of the Sultai would like to know too.

scene.line: The Way has no beginning and no end. It is simply the path.
Our own selves are the greatest obstacles to enlightenment.
Prowess: whenever you cast a noncreature spell, a creature with prowess gets +1/+1 until end of turn. Cast your spells before you attack.

villainScene.line: If weakness does not exist within the Temur then we shall force it upon them.
The best servants are made from those who died without a scratch.

after.line: The voice you hear is Ugin, the spirit dragon. His bones lie in a tomb of their own. Go, and be careful what you ask him for.

battles.title: A Thousand Years Ago
battles.blurb: At the tomb, Ugin's voice pulls Sarkhan back more than a thousand years. The clans are young, the dragon tempests still rage, and Yasova Dragonclaw of the Temur is fighting Tasigur, the Sultai khan, who has expensive taste in zombies.

scene.line: All at once Sarkhan's mind fell silent.
As the clans carved out their territories, we saw allies where the Mardu saw only obstacles.
Delve: their big creatures exile cards from their graveyard to pay for themselves. An empty graveyard makes them expensive again.

villainScene.line: They were your friends, your family, your clan. They want only to welcome you.
No machinations, no puppet strings, no plots. Just pure, sweeping death.

after.line: Her hunger knows no limit. Left unchecked, she would feast on all of Tarkir.
She means Atarka, a dragon. We have more dragons than we can kill. Why would anyone want to save one?

battles.title: The Traitor Returns
battles.blurb: Before the tomb, there is Zurgo. Sarkhan was once a Mardu warrior and then walked away, and Zurgo Helmsmasher, khan of the Mardu, has made a legend out of hating him.

scene.line: No body can contain so much fury. It reminds me of another battle, long past.
Raid: their raid cards get a bonus if they attacked this turn. Make every attack cost them something.

villainScene.line: You have returned from fire, traitor. This time I will see you leave as ashes.
Do you hear that, Sarkhan? The glory of the horde! I made a legend from what you abandoned.
I came seeking a challenge. All I found was you.

after.line: He will never stop. Neither will the voice. Only one of them is worth following.

battles.title: Ugin's Fate
battles.blurb: Sarkhan reaches the place where Ugin fell after his battle with Nicol Bolas. Ugin is dying. Dragons are circling, and Sarkhan has to hold them off long enough to seal Ugin into a hedron.

scene.line: Ugin's whispered summons led Sarkhan Vol to the moment that would echo down the centuries and seal Tarkir's fate: the primal battle between Ugin and Nicol Bolas.
Every choice alters the path of fate.
Manifest: put the top card of your library onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2. If it is a creature, you can turn it face up for its mana cost.

villainScene.line: She answers the call of the Crave, the desire for battle sated only by bloodshed.
Kolaghan's army rushes from kill to kill, desperate to avoid the dragon's wrath.

after.line: Sarkhan closes the hedron around the broken dragon. Somewhere behind him, a thousand years start to change.

battles.title: Siege Rhino
battles.blurb: The Archive remembers Khans Standard: Abzan midrange and its Siege Rhinos, against Jeskai decks that made an army of tokens out of cheap spells.

deck.name: Abzan
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from cards in this act's sets only, so Courser of Kruphix, Sylvan Caryatid, Hero's Downfall and Elspeth, Sun's Champion are not in it.

scene.line: The mere approach of an Abzan war beast is enough to send enemies fleeing in panic.
Outlast: pay the cost and tap the creature to put a +1/+1 counter on it, any time you could cast a sorcery. Slow, but it adds up.

after.line: Recorded: Khans of Tarkir Standard, 2014 to 2015.

battles.title: Atarka's Command
battles.blurb: The Archive remembers summer 2015: Atarka Red, which tried to win on turn four with tokens and pump spells, against Esper Dragons and its counterspells.

scene.line: Atarka serving-goblins coat themselves with grease imbued with noxious herbs, hoping to discourage their ravenous masters from adding them to the meal.
Go wide, then pump everything at once. Do not give the dragons time to land.

villainScene.line: Attracting a dragon's attention may be the last mistake you make.

battles.title: Dragonlord Silumgar
battles.blurb: Sarkhan wakes in a Tarkir ruled by dragons. In the swamps, Dragonlord Silumgar sits on a mountain of treasure with Sidisi as his vizier. Sarkhan and Narset go to see the new world's worst dragon.

scene.line: In the Tarkir I once knew, the Abzan revered their ancestor trees. Now, as Dromoka, they cut their finest groves to make weapons.
Abzan, Jeskai, Sultai, Mardu, Temur—names lost to history, yet worthy of further study.
He takes what you have and keeps it. Make him spend his cards, then spend yours.

villainScene.line: Bring forth the dead, their skull-grins and rattle-bones. We will feast upon their wailing ghosts.
The most profound secrets lie in the darkest places of the world. It can be prudent to make use of another set of eyes.
The realization that one is dying is far more terrifying than death itself.

half.line: He is greedy, not careful. Keep making him choose.

battles.title: Treasure Cruise
battles.blurb: Deep in the archive, the card that made a cruise ship cost one blue mana.

archive.what: Cheap red and blue tempo decks that filled the graveyard with one-mana spells, then cast Treasure Cruise and Dig Through Time for one or two mana by delving it away.
archive.why: Delve made an eight-mana card cost almost nothing in the right deck, and the older formats had the right decks.
archive.beat: Race them and kill the small creatures. Their card draw is only cheap once the graveyard is full.
archive.after: Treasure Cruise and Dig Through Time were banned in Modern in January 2015. This tribute follows the Vintage list, so it plays one of each.

deck.name: Treasure Cruise Tempo
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from cards in this act's sets only. No single tournament list is copied.

scene.line: Countless delights drift on the surface while dark schemes run below.
Kill the Swiftspears. Make them pay full price.

villainScene.line: The calligraphy of combat is written with strokes of sudden blood.

after.line: Recorded: Treasure Cruise and Dig Through Time, banned in Modern in January 2015.
